message.content:
Here are some of the most popular books written by J.K. Rowling:

| Series / Title | Publication Year | Notes |
|----------------|------------------|-------|
| **Harry Potter** (7‑book series) | 1997–2007 | *Philosopher’s Stone* (UK)/*Sorcerer’s Stone* (US), *Chamber of Secrets*, *Prisoner of Azkaban*, *Goblet of Fire*, *Order of the Phoenix*, *Half‑Blood Prince*, *Deathly Hallows*. These fantasy novels follow the young wizard Harry Potter as he battles the dark wizard Voldemort. They have sold over 500 million copies worldwide and were adapted into a hugely successful film franchise. |
| **Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them** | 2001 (novelization) | A companion book to the films, presented as a textbook used by Hogwarts students. It was later expanded into a new film series set before the events of Harry Potter. |
| **Quidditch Through the Ages** | 2001 | Another Hogwarts textbook, detailing the history of Quidditch. |
| **The Tales of Beedle the Bard** | 2008 | A collection of children’s fairy tales within the wizarding world, referenced in *Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows*. |
| **The Casual Vacancy** | 2012 | Rowling’s first adult novel published under her own name. It’s a contemporary drama set in a small English town, exploring social issues and political intrigue. |
| **Cormoran Strike** series (written as Robert Galbraith) | 2013–present | Starting with *The Cuckoo’s Calling*, this detective mystery series follows private investigator Cormoran Strike and his assistant Robin Ellacott. The books have been well received and adapted into a BBC television series. |

These titles represent the breadth of Rowling’s work—from the beloved Harry Potter saga to her ventures into adult fiction and crime thrillers.
